text: The Patriots dominated the Pittsburgh Steelers 20-3 in their Week 2 home opener at Gillette Stadium, with TreVeyon Henderson punching in a touchdown and the defense suffocating Pittsburgh's offense in man coverage, though film review of Drake Maye's performance revealed the rookie still has work to do in consistently executing the offensive system that carried New England to a Super Bowl run last season. The victory came at a cost: starting right guard Mike Onwenu suffered a broken right ankle that will impact the offensive line going forward, adding to what was otherwise a banged-up performance from the Patriots roster. Despite the defensive prowess and the win itself, Head Coach Mike Vrabel and his team have yet to establish the offensive rhythm necessary to sustain a championship-caliber campaign, suggesting that while the unit can lean on its defense to win games, the offensive consistency must improve for this team to reach the heights it achieved in 2025.
